about: Provider compatibility matrix rendered on the landing page and /docs/providers/. Edit by hand when a provider's state changes, then run `python scripts/site_facts.py` (it validates this file) and rebuild the site. `label` is the row's overall state; `execution.status` is the isolated `repo-ai do` path only. label EXECUTION requires execution.status EXECUTION with a dated, versioned observation.

labels.EXECUTION: repo-ai runs it as an isolated mission provider (repo-ai do), and a live, independently re-verified change has been observed.
labels.HOST_ONLY: repo-ai wires context, rules, skills and hooks into it (repo-ai init), but cannot run it as an isolated provider.
labels.CONTEXT_SKILLS_ONLY: repo-ai writes context and skills files the tool can read; no hooks and no isolated execution.
labels.PLANNED: Intended, not implemented. Nothing on this site claims it works.
labels.BLOCKED: Tried, and stopped by an external blocker (authentication, account or terms) that is named.
labels.UNSUPPORTED: Not supported, and not planned for now.

providers.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
providers.label: EXECUTION

execution.observed: Live, independently re-verified change through repo-ai do on the published 0.10.0 wheel (2026-10-30, hidden oracle 17/17, undo byte-exact), with the 0.10.0 sandbox that hides the rest of HOME. Runs inside repo-ai's outer sandbox with Codex's own sandbox bypassed, only once the outer one is confirmed. Disclosed: the login token copied into its sandbox is readable by a model with shell access; use a separate repo-ai login (repo-ai agents setup codex). Opt-in from 0.11.3 (REPO_AI_CODEX_BROKER=1, macOS): a credential broker keeps the token outside the sandbox and limits Codex to one loopback port. It was live-verified on 2026-10-31 with a ChatGPT login on a development build (two runs; an API-key login is not yet verified).
execution.platforms: macOS (seatbelt) verified live; Linux bubblewrap path covered by tests, no live mission this cycle

providers.name: Claude Code
providers.label: EXECUTION

execution.observed: Live, independently re-verified changes through repo-ai do on the published 0.10.0 wheel (2026-10-30): mission PASS, hidden oracle 17/17, apply and undo byte-exact, and a hostile-repository run whose injected instructions were not followed. Uses Claude Code's own login, nothing copied: a separate repo-ai login (live-verified) or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from claude setup-token (not yet live-verified). The model gets file tools only, and every live run first checks, at no cost, that the session would load nothing else.
execution.platforms: macOS (seatbelt) verified live; Linux bubblewrap profile covered by tests, not live-verified

providers.host: Fully supported as a host: repo-ai init --agent claude writes a marked CLAUDE.md block, path-scoped rules, curated skills and hooks that attach ranked context to prompts.
providers.cost: Claude's own USD cap via --max-cost-usd, checked between turns (one turn of overshoot observed); on a subscription the reported cost is notional

execution.observed: OpenCode against a local, loopback-only model endpoint (Ollama), account-free. On the published 0.10.0 wheel (2026-10-30) with qwen3:8b: one attempt refused (broken edit), one PASS of the visible tests that a hidden case failed (the model dropped a docstring requirement no test pinned); on development builds 1 of 4 passed. repo-ai refused every broken candidate. Deny-by-default tools, network to loopback only. Network note (measured 2026-10-31): no other host is reachable, but on macOS seatbelt's loopback rule also admits the machine's own network addresses and lets the agent listen on every interface.
execution.platforms: macOS only (no tested restriction elsewhere: refused)

providers.name: OpenCode over ACP (local model)
providers.label: EXECUTION

execution.observed: OpenCode driven over the Agent Client Protocol (`opencode acp`) under exactly the opencode isolation: seatbelt, scratch HOME, deny-by-default inline config, loopback-only network. The ACP client stays outside the sandbox and serves file reads and writes only within the run's paths. Any protocol problem, refusal, timeout or stop reason other than end_turn fails the run, and OpenCode's own edit is still checked. Live $0 on a development build (2026-10-31, qwen3:8b): PASS on a scratch fixture in 60 s. Network note (measured 2026-10-31): no other host is reachable, but on macOS seatbelt's loopback rule also admits the machine's own network addresses and lets the agent listen on every interface.
